parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by the luminosity of a star.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how standard candles are used to determine the distance to a galaxy.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
The Sun rotates on its axis. Points X, Y and Z are on the equator of the Sun as shown in Fig. 10.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The wavelengths of light from points X and Y are observed and recorded in Table 10.1.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text:
The Sun rotates with a period of 2.07 × 10⁶ s.

Show that the radius of the Sun is 6.93 × 10⁸ m.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain how the expected wavelength of the light observed from Z compares with the emitted wavelength.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The luminosity of the Sun is 3.8 × 10²⁶ W.

Use the information in (b)(i) to calculate the surface temperature of the Sun.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.1
figures.alt: A diagram of the Sun with a vertical axis of rotation and a horizontal equator, showing points X, Y and Z and the direction of rotation.

figures.caption: Table 10.1
figures.alt: A table gives observed wavelengths of 656.2877 nm from X and 656.2831 nm from Y.
